conceptCapsule.title: Inclined Plane Projectiles & Uniform Circular Motion (UCM)
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Projectile on Incline: Choosing axes along the incline ($x'$) and normal to the incline ($y'$): $a_{x'} = \mp g\sin\beta$ ($-$ for up, $+$ for down), $a_{y'} = -g\cos\beta$. Time of flight: $T = \frac{2u\sin\alpha}{g\cos\beta}$. Maximum range up plane: $R_{\max, \text{up}} = \frac{u^2}{g(1+\sin\beta)}$ at $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\beta}{2}$. Perpendicular impact condition: $\tan\alpha = \frac{\cot\beta}{2}$. 2. Uniform Circular Motion: Angular speed $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = 2\pi f$. Linear speed $v = \omega R$. Centripetal acceleration $\vec{a}_c = -\omega^2\vec{r} = -\frac{v^2}{R}\hat{r}$. Momentum change over angle $\theta$: $|\Delta\vec{p}| = 2mv\sin(\theta/2)$.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: In UCM, the speed and kinetic energy are strictly scalar constants, but velocity, linear momentum, and acceleration vectors are continuously changing due to direction change. For inclined planes, remember that the perpendicular collision condition requires $v_{x'} = 0$ at landing, leading to $\tan\alpha = \frac{\cot\beta}{2}$.

questions.statement: A particle is projected from the base of an inclined plane of inclination $\beta$ with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\alpha$ relative to the inclined surface. The time of flight $T$ is:
questions.solution:
Taking axis perpendicular to the incline with acceleration $a_{y'} = -g\cos\beta$ and initial component $u_{y'} = u\sin\alpha$: $$(u\sin\alpha)T - \frac{1}{2}(g\cos\beta)T^2 = 0 \implies T = \frac{2u\sin\alpha}{g\cos\beta}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: For a given projection speed $u$ up an inclined plane of inclination $\beta$, the angle of projection $\alpha$ with the incline that maximizes the range up the plane is:
questions.solution:
Range up the plane is $R = \frac{u^2}{g\cos^2\beta}[\sin(2\alpha + \beta) - \sin\beta]$. Range is maximum when $\sin(2\alpha + \beta) = 1 \implies 2\alpha + \beta = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies \alpha = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\beta}{2}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected up an incline of angle $\beta = 30^\circ$ with speed $u$. If it strikes the inclined plane perpendicularly, the angle of projection $\alpha$ with respect to the incline satisfies:
questions.solution:
1. Condition for perpendicular impact: $v_{x'} = 0 \implies u\cos\alpha - (g\sin\beta)T = 0$.
2. Substituting $T = \frac{2u\sin\alpha}{g\cos\beta}$: $u\cos\alpha = 2u\sin\alpha\tan\beta \implies \tan\alpha = \frac{\cot\beta}{2}$.
3. For $\beta = 30^\circ$, $\cot(30^\circ) = \sqrt{3} \implies \tan\alpha = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ (or $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}$ depending on reference).
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: The maximum range $R_{\max}$ of a projectile fired down an inclined plane of inclination $\beta$ with speed $u$ is:
questions.solution:
For projection down an incline: $$R_{\max} = \frac{u^2(1 + \sin\beta)}{g\cos^2\beta} = \frac{u^2(1 + \sin\beta)}{g(1 - \sin^2\beta)} = \frac{u^2}{g(1 - \sin\beta)}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in a circle of radius $r = 0.5\text{ m}$ with a constant angular speed $\omega = 4\text{ rad/s}$. The linear speed $v$ and centripetal acceleration $a_c$ of the particle are:
questions.solution:
1. Linear speed: $v = r\omega = 0.5 \times 4 = 2\text{ m/s}$.
2. Centripetal acceleration: $a_c = \omega^2 r = 4^2 \times 0.5 = 8\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in uniform circular motion of radius $R$. If its time period of revolution is $T$, the magnitude of average acceleration during half a revolution is:
questions.solution:
1. In half a revolution ($\Delta t = T/2$), velocity vector reverses: $|\Delta\vec{v}| = 2v = 2\left(\frac{2\pi R}{T}\right) = \frac{4\pi R}{T}$.
2. Average acceleration: $a_{\text{avg}} = \frac{|\Delta\vec{v}|}{\Delta t} = \frac{4\pi R / T}{T / 2} = \frac{8\pi R}{T^2}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: For a particle in uniform circular motion, the position vector $\vec{r}$ and centripetal acceleration vector $\vec{a}_c$ satisfy which relation?
questions.solution:
The centripetal acceleration is radially directed inward towards the center, exactly opposite to the outward position vector $\vec{r}$: $$\vec{a}_c = -\omega^2\vec{r}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is executing uniform circular motion of radius $R$ with constant speed $v$. The change in momentum of the particle in traversing an arc subtending an angle $\theta$ at the center is:
questions.solution:
$$|\Delta\vec{p}| = \sqrt{p^2 + p^2 - 2p^2\cos\theta} = p\sqrt{2(1-\cos\theta)} = 2p\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2mv\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The minute hand of a clock has a length of $6\text{ cm}$. The magnitude of the displacement vector and average velocity of the tip of the minute hand from $12:00\text{ PM}$ to $12:30\text{ PM}$ are:
questions.solution:
1. Displacement across diameter: $d = 2 \times 6 = 12\text{ cm}$.
2. Time elapsed $\Delta t = 30 \times 60 = 1800\text{ s}$.
3. Average velocity: $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{12\text{ cm}}{1800\text{ s}} = \frac{1}{150}\text{ cm/s}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A body is projected from an incline of angle $\beta$ with velocity $u$ at angle $\alpha$ to the incline. The maximum height $H_{\max}$ reached above the inclined surface is:
questions.solution:
Using $v_{y'}^2 = u_{y'}^2 - 2a_{y'}H_{\max}$ with $v_{y'} = 0$ at peak: $$0 = (u\sin\alpha)^2 - 2(g\cos\beta)H_{\max} \implies H_{\max} = \frac{u^2\sin^2\alpha}{2g\cos\beta}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: If a body is executing uniform circular motion, which of the following quantities remains strictly constant?
questions.solution:
In uniform circular motion, speed $v$ is constant, so scalar kinetic energy $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ remains constant. Vectors $\vec{v}, \vec{a}, \vec{p}$ continuously change direction.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in a circle of radius $20\text{ cm}$ at $120\text{ rpm}$. The magnitude of its centripetal acceleration is: (Take $\pi^2 \approx 9.87$)
questions.solution:
1. $\omega = 120 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 4\pi\text{ rad/s}$.
2. $a_c = \omega^2 r = (4\pi)^2 \times 0.2 = 16\pi^2 \times 0.2 = 3.2\pi^2\text{ m/s}^2 \approx 31.58\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ move in concentric circles of radii $R_P$ and $R_Q$ with the same time period $T$. The ratio of their centripetal accelerations $\dfrac{a_P}{a_Q}$ is:
questions.solution:
Centripetal acceleration $a_c = \omega^2 R = \left(\frac{2\pi}{T}\right)^2 R$. Since $T$ is identical, $\frac{a_P}{a_Q} = \frac{R_P}{R_Q}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected from the ground with speed $u$ up an inclined plane of inclination $\beta$. The ratio of the maximum range up the plane to the maximum range down the plane for the same launch speed $u$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{R_{\max, \text{up}}}{R_{\max, \text{down}}} = \frac{\frac{u^2}{g(1+\sin\beta)}}{\frac{u^2}{g(1-\sin\beta)}} = \frac{1 - \sin\beta}{1 + \sin\beta}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: An object moves along a circular path of radius $R$ in uniform circular motion with linear momentum $p$. The centripetal force acting on the object is given by:
questions.solution:
Since $p = mv \implies v = p/m$: $$F_c = \frac{mv^2}{R} = \frac{m(p/m)^2}{R} = \frac{p^2}{mR}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle projected from the base of an incline of angle $\beta$ lands at the same level of the incline after time $T$. The horizontal component of displacement is given by:
questions.solution:
The range $R$ lies along the incline surface inclined at angle $ eta$ to the horizontal. Resolving horizontally gives $x = R\cos\beta$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: If angular displacement of a rotating wheel varies with time as $\theta(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2\text{ rad}$, the angular acceleration at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\omega(t) = \frac{d\theta}{dt} = 6t^2 - 6t$.
2. $\alpha(t) = \frac{d\omega}{dt} = 12t - 6$.
3. $\alpha(2) = 12(2) - 6 = 18\text{ rad/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A wheel of radius $R = 0.4\text{ m}$ rotates with constant angular speed $\omega = 10\text{ rad/s}$. The distance traveled by a point on the rim in $5\text{ seconds}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Linear speed: $v = \omega R = 10 \times 0.4 = 4\text{ m/s}$.
2. Distance in $5\text{ s}$: $s = v \times t = 4 \times 5 = 20\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: For an inclined plane of inclination $\beta$, a projectile is thrown up the plane. If the initial velocity is purely perpendicular to the incline ($\alpha = 90^\circ$), the time of flight $T$ is:
questions.solution:
$$T = \frac{2u\sin 90^\circ}{g\cos\beta} = \frac{2u}{g\cos\beta}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A projectile is launched down an inclined plane of angle $30^\circ$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the incline with speed $u = 10\text{ m/s}$. The range along the incline is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. $T = \frac{2(10)\sin 30^\circ}{10\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\text{ s}$.
2. $R = u_{x'}T + \frac{1}{2}a_{x'}T^2 = (10\cos 30^\circ)\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \frac{1}{2}(10\sin 30^\circ)\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = 10 + \frac{10}{3} = \frac{40}{3}\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
